Compile one remote-sensing question into taskgraph-v1.1-dsl-v1. Return only the
DSL program: no JSON, Markdown, explanation, or predicted answer. The input JSON
contains question, coarse question_type, original choices, and image inputs.
Never copy choices into the program or use a ground-truth answer.

Use only $image0, $image1, ... and sequential n1, n2, ... references. Emit an
optional INTENT(enum), one contributing node per line, then exactly one
FINAL(source-or-list,answer_type) or
FINAL_QUESTION(source-or-list,answer_type,"static residual question"). Final
sources must be $nX references, never raw images.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),
SELECT_REL, SELECT_RANK, SELECT_ORD, SELECT_EXTREME, SELECT_SUBREGION, GROUP,
COUNT, COUNT_IMAGE, COUNT_ENTITIES, ATTRIBUTE, CLASSIFY, MULTILABEL_CLASSIFY,
MOTION, RELATION, ABS_DIFF, VLM_REASON, BUILD_ROUTE_CONTEXT, and ROUTE_REASON.
Follow the canonical argument roles learned from the examples; use JSON strings,
true/false/null, enum symbols, lists, and T("category",attribute=value).

Prefer dedicated deterministic operators over VLM_REASON. COUNT is mandatory
and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. Use FINAL_QUESTION only when visual or
semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include runtime values.

CHOICE_MULTI is indeterminate multi-select: the downstream Choice VLM selects
every applicable option and may return one or more ids. CHOICE_SINGLE permits
exactly one id. Infer this from question semantics, never legacy question_type
cardinality labels.

{"choices":["(A) White","(B) Blue","(C) Red","(D) Green","(E) This image doesn't feature the color."],"inputs":{"image0":{"type":"image","uri_or_key":"remote_sensing/dota_v2_dota_v2_dota_v2_P10271.png"}},"question":"What color is the car at the top of the road in the middle of the picture?","question_type":"MULTIPLE_CHOICE"}

INTENT(ATTRIBUTE_QUERY)
n1=REGION($image0,CENTER)
n2=LOCATE($n1,T("road"))
n3=LOCATE($n1,T("car"))
n4=SELECT_REL($n3,$n2,NEAR)
n5=SELECT_ORD($n4,null,1,TOP_TO_BOTTOM)
n6=ATTRIBUTE($n5,"color")
FINAL($n6,CHOICE_SINGLE)

{"choices":["(A) red","(B) black","(C) blue","(D) yellow","(E) This image doesn't feature the color."],"inputs":{"image0":{"type":"image","uri_or_key":"remote_sensing/dota_v2_dota_v2_dota_v2_P4077.png"}},"question":"What color is the car in the bottom right corner of the first parking lot on the far left side of the picture?","question_type":"MULTIPLE_CHOICE"}

INTENT(ATTRIBUTE_QUERY)
n1=REGION($image0,LEFT)
n2=LOCATE($n1,T("parking lot"))
n3=SELECT_ORD($n2,null,1,LEFT_TO_RIGHT)
n4=LOCATE($image0,T("car"))
n5=SELECT_REL($n4,$n3,INSIDE)
FINAL_QUESTION([$n3,$n5],CHOICE_SINGLE,"What color is the car in the bottom right corner of the selected parking lot?")

Compile one remote-sensing question into taskgraph-v1.1-dsl-v1. Return only the
DSL program: no JSON, Markdown, explanation, or predicted answer. The input JSON
contains question, coarse question_type, original choices, and image inputs.
Never copy choices into the program or use a ground-truth answer.

Use only $image0, $image1, ... and sequential n1, n2, ... references. Emit an
optional INTENT(enum), one contributing node per line, then exactly one
FINAL(source-or-list,answer_type) or
FINAL_QUESTION(source-or-list,answer_type,"static residual question"). Final
sources must be $nX references, never raw images.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),
SELECT_REL, SELECT_RANK, SELECT_ORD, SELECT_EXTREME, SELECT_SUBREGION, GROUP,
COUNT, COUNT_IMAGE, COUNT_ENTITIES, ATTRIBUTE, CLASSIFY, MULTILABEL_CLASSIFY,
MOTION, RELATION, ABS_DIFF, VLM_REASON, BUILD_ROUTE_CONTEXT, and ROUTE_REASON.
Follow the canonical argument roles learned from the examples; use JSON strings,
true/false/null, enum symbols, lists, and T("category",attribute=value).

Prefer dedicated deterministic operators over VLM_REASON. COUNT is mandatory
and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. Use FINAL_QUESTION only when visual or
semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include runtime values.

CHOICE_MULTI is indeterminate multi-select: the downstream Choice VLM selects
every applicable option and may return one or more ids. CHOICE_SINGLE permits
exactly one id. Infer this from question semantics, never legacy question_type
cardinality labels.

{"choices":["(A) Port","(B) Multi-unit residential buildings","(C) Airport Terminal","(D) Parking Lot or Garage"],"inputs":{"image0":{"type":"image","uri_or_key":"DOTA_v2_4096_4096/dota_v2_dota_v2_dota_v2_P11097.png"}},"question":"Select the options that best represent the types of land use depicted in the image.","question_type":"MULTIPLE_CHOICE"}

INTENT(MULTILABEL_CLASSIFICATION)
n1=MULTILABEL_CLASSIFY($image0,["(A) Port","(B) Multi-unit residential buildings","(C) Airport Terminal","(D) Parking Lot or Garage"])
FINAL($n1,CHOICE_MULTI)

metadata.source_category: Land use classification/Overall Land use classification

{"choices":["(A) Red Containers","(B) Orange Buildings","(C) White buildings","(D) Green Buildings"],"inputs":{"image0":{"type":"image","uri_or_key":"MiniFrance/44-2013-0350-6700-LA93-0M50-E080.jp2.tif"}},"question":"Identify the object category within the given bounding box in the satellite or aerial image. Image resolution: 10000 x 10000. Bounding box: [5155, 7378, 5203, 7411].","question_type":"MULTIPLE_CHOICE"}

INTENT(OBJECT_CLASSIFICATION)
n1=REGION_BBOX($image0,[5155.0,7378.0,5203.0,7411.0])
n2=CLASSIFY($n1)
FINAL($n2,CHOICE_SINGLE)

{"choices":["(A) 30","(B) 29","(C) 28","(D) 26"],"inputs":{"image0":{"type":"image","uri_or_key":"HRSCD-2012-3/35-2012-0345-6770-LA93-0M50-E080-1.png"}},"question":"How many houses are there within the red circled area?","question_type":"MULTIPLE_CHOICE"}

INTENT(SIMPLE_COUNT)
n1=FIND_MARKER($image0,"circle","red")
n2=COUNT($n1,T("house"),false)
FINAL($n2,CHOICE_SINGLE)
